title: Turnip and pork fritters with figs

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Everything is a whole food or a plain staple: turnips, pork mince, eggs, flour, oil, figs, rocket and balsamic.

supermarket.reason: Fresh figs are a bit pricier than the rest, but Tesco stocks them in small packs in autumn, and everything else is an everyday item.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a grater, a bowl, a tea towel and a frying pan, and grating and shallow frying are well within a beginner's reach.

works.reason: Squeezed turnip bound with egg, flour and pork mince makes a firm mix, and thin spoonfuls fried 4 to 5 minutes a side will cook the pork through, giving a fair lunch for four.

honest_times.reason: Twenty-five minutes covers peeling and grating 400g of turnip, slicing, chopping and mixing, and the 30 minutes matches the 10-minute salting plus two frying batches.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning, including the sage, is used in the steps, and nothing unlisted appears.

seasonal_feel.reason: Grated turnip is the body of the fritters, which suits early October, and figs and rocket are both in season then.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are brief, plain British instructions a neighbour would give.

hearty_healthy.reason: It is a filling lunch of vegetables, pork and egg with a fresh salad, the kind of thing a family would happily eat again.
